subject: Production: Streaming timeouts & chunked transfer failures — FastPay
messages:
From: Olivia Zhang <olivia@fastpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: FastPay Platform Team <platform@fastpay.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed streaming hangs during peak writes

Sean —

We're seeing repeated streaming stalls and eventual timeouts from our integration with Redwood starting ~08:50 PDT. The client receives partial chunks for ~30–90s, then the connection drops with a chunked-transfer error or WebSocket close (1006) depending on the path. This is affecting our payment-validation UX; throughput drops by ~45% during the window.

Attached: fastpay_stream_trace_0518.log and websocket_tracechunks.zip (includes browser-side traces and server-side accept logs).

We need immediate next steps — this is blocking our rollout. Can your team triage urgently and share a mitigation we can apply from our side while you investigate?

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay

--
FastPay | https://www.fastpay.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed streaming hangs during peak writes

Olivia —

Thanks for the traces and the heads-up. We're escalating to engineering immediately. Preliminary ask: can you confirm whether you're connecting to the WebSocket endpoint (wss://stream.redwood.ai) or using chunked HTTP streaming via our REST stream endpoint? You mentioned both in the logs.

Action plan (first 1 hour):
- Marcus is taking lead on server-side traces and proxy timeouts.
- Marissa will coordinate a brief phone call and capture exact timestamps from your side.
- I will loop in our infra lead if we need to change ingress timeouts or add a temporary non-streaming fallback.

Temporary mitigation you can try: switch to the polling 'batch' endpoint ([non-streaming]) for critical requests if possible (loses low-latency streaming but avoids the hang). I'll confirm how quickly we can toggle a routing fallback from our side.

I'll update in ~30–45 minutes with findings.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Zhang <olivia@fastpay.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed streaming hangs during peak writes

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 9:28 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Olivia —
>
> Thanks for the traces and the heads-up. We're escalating to engineering immediately.

I've pulled the logs (fastpay_stream_trace_0518.log). Early indicators: repeated TCP FINs from our ingress followed by a proxy reset. The pattern suggests the upstream worker is stalling on flush and the nginx-ingress / envoy timeout is closing the connection.

Suspected causes:
- Long-running tokenization / attention spikes for certain inputs producing backpressure beyond our default keepalive/window settings.
- Proxy (envoy/nginx) send_timeout/read_timeout defaults (30s) being triggered under partial-chunk flush patterns.
- Client/browser-side connection retry logic giving up after intermittent 1006 closes.

Immediate mitigations we can deploy (30–90 min):
1) Increase ingress send_timeout/read_timeout to 120s for the affected route.
2) Enable streaming chunk flush policy: force smaller flush intervals to avoid large buffered chunk sizes.
3) Temporarily route FastPay to a dedicated routing shard (reduced concurrency) to see if throughput/backpressure correlation improves.

I will run a quick test patch to increase the timeout and enable more aggressive chunk flushing on a canary. Need a short maintenance window — Marissa, can you confirm if FastPay can tolerate a 5–10 minute window now?

—Marcus
Principal Backend Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@fastpay.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observed streaming hangs during peak writes

Olivia — quick call?

We can do a rolling canary now that increases the ingress timeouts and toggles chunk-flush to smaller intervals. If you can provide a 10-minute maintenance window in the next 30 minutes we will run the canary and iterate. If your workload cannot tolerate any interruption, tell us and we will instead enable dedicated routing without touching production timeouts.

Also noting: this is hitting your production route and correlates with a FastPay traffic spike at ~08:45. We will monitor token-level latency and error-rate delta and revert if errors increase.

Logan — looping you in because this is customer-impacting and may need executive engagement for SLA considerations.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

We appreciate the fast escalation. I will keep this on my radar until the canary is validated. If we need to provide a short-term credit or SLA accommodation, let me know the business impact metrics and I will coordinate. Logan Wright

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Zhang <olivia@fastpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final update: increased timeouts + chunk-flush canary results

Olivia / team —

Post-mortem update: we deployed the canary (ingress read/send timeouts increased from 30s to 120s and chunk-flush set to 200–300ms) and observed immediate improvement in streamed responses — hangs went from ~6 events/hour to near zero on the canary shard. After monitoring for 24 hours, we rolled the change to your primary routing shard at 15:30 PDT on 2026-05-20.

Key findings:
- The underlying cause was a combination of large model outputs for a small set of prompts that produced bursty KV-cache writes and delayed flushes, plus ingress timeouts treated as hard closes.
- The chunked transfer behaviour (large buffered writes without intermediate flushes) triggered proxy-level timeouts, causing 1006 WebSocket closures and chunked transfer errors in browsers.

Actions taken:
- Increased ingress timeouts to 120s for your route (permanent for now, can revert with safe guard thresholds).
- Enabled aggressive chunk flush for streaming outputs on your shard.
- Added a routing fallback flag so we can switch FastPay to non-streaming batch endpoints automatically if we detect repeat stalls.
- Collected traces and attached the sanitized logs to the HubSpot incident.

Next steps / recommendations for FastPay:
- If you can, add client-side retry with exponential backoff for 1006 closes and consider a short keepalive ping every 15–20s.
- If you continue to see stalls tied to specific prompts, share the prompt set and we can recommend model/quantization profile changes.

Marissa will follow up on SLA credit requests and any additional support. Let us know if you want a summary post-mortem and timeline for your execs.

Thanks for patience and for sharing traces early — that materially reduced TTR.

—Sean
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nginx_ingress_timings.txt (sanitized), fastpay_stream_trace_0518.log (sanitized), websocket_tracechunks.zip (sanitized)
